controls.aicm_title: Audit and Assurance Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain audit and assurance policies and procedures and standards. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance: establish/document/approve/maintain audit policies and review them annually. CAIQ confirms it asks whether policies exist and are reviewed, not any infrastructure configuration property. No config posture component; nothing for a snapshot evaluator to verify.

controls.aicm_specification: Conduct independent audit and assurance assessments according to relevant standards at least annually.
controls.notes: Requires conducting independent audits per relevant standards on a schedule. Human/process activity (assessment cadence and independence), not a configuration property of any cloud resource. Not config-verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Perform independent audit and assurance assessments according to risk-based plans and policies, and in response to significant changes or emerging risks.
controls.notes: Risk-based audit planning and triggering assessments on significant changes is a program/process matter. No resource configuration to evaluate; out of scope for a static-snapshot evaluator.

controls.aicm_specification: Verify compliance with all relevant standards, regulations, legal/contractual, and statutory requirements applicable to the audit.
controls.notes: Verifying legal/contractual/statutory compliance applicable to the audit is a governance activity spanning many domains. While individual technical requirements may be checked by Stave controls elsewhere, this control itself is the organizational obligation to verify compliance, not a discrete config property. Out of scope organizationally.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement an Audit Management process aligned with relevant auditing standards, to support audit planning, risk analysis, security control assessment, conclusion, remediation schedules, report generation, and review of past reports and supporting evidence.
controls.notes: Defining and operating an audit management process (planning, risk analysis, reporting, evidence review) is process design. No cloud-config property to assert; out of scope for snapshot evaluation.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain a risk-based corrective action plan to remediate audit findings, regularly review and report remediation status to relevant stakeholders.
controls.notes: Corrective-action-plan lifecycle and remediation-status reporting to stakeholders is an organizational process. No configuration property to evaluate from a snapshot; out of scope organizationally.

controls.aicm_title: Application and Interface Security Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures for application security. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance: establish/document/approve/communicate/review-annually policy and procedures. No technical config artifact in a cloud snapshot expresses whether an application-security policy document exists or was reviewed.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document and maintain baseline requirements for securing applications.
controls.notes: Documentation of baseline requirements is a human/process artifact. The enforcement of specific baselines maps to other AICM controls (AIS-08/09/12) and their Stave controls, but the existence/maintenance of the baseline document itself is not config-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement technical and operational metrics in alignment with business objectives, security requirements, and compliance obligations.
controls.notes: Defining/tracking security metrics and aligning them to business objectives is a governance/operations activity. No cloud configuration property captures whether an organization defines and reports application-security metrics.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement a secure SDLC process for application requirements analysis, planning, design, development, testing, deployment, and operation in accordance with security requirements.
controls.notes: Secure SDLC is a process program. Individual technical enforcement points it mandates (code review, static analysis, testing, secure deploy) are config-verifiable and map under AIS-05/AIS-06/AIS-12, but the SDLC process definition itself is organizational and not derivable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement a testing strategy, including criteria for acceptance of new  information systems, upgrades and new versions, which provides  application security assurance and maintains compliance while meeting  organizational delivery goals.  Automate when applicable and possible.
controls.notes: Config-verifiable slice: Stave confirms automated security testing is wired in (image/artifact vulnerability scanning enabled, dependency scanning on, Inspector enabled and covering hosts, branch status checks required before merge). Missing/organizational: the testing STRATEGY itself, defined acceptance criteria for new systems/upgrades, SAST/DAST tool configuration and gating thresholds, and whether tests actually pass. Those are process artifacts no snapshot encodes.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and implement strategies and capabilities for secure, standardized, and compliant application deployment. Automate where possible.
controls.notes: Config-verifiable slice: Stave hardens the standardized deploy pipeline (CodeBuild buildspec not user-controlled, no privileged Docker, no plaintext secrets, least-privilege/scoped build roles, no embedded source creds, anchored webhook filters, required status checks, immutable releases, controlled stage auto-deploy, CI/CD role separation). Missing/organizational: the overall deployment STRATEGY, change-management/approval gating, and 'compliant' attestation of each deploy are process concerns not in a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement a process to remediate application security vulnerabilities, automating remediation when possible.
controls.notes: Config-verifiable slice: Stave detects unremediated findings aging past threshold (Inspector findings stale, patch scan stale) and that the detection prerequisites exist (Inspector/ECR scanning enabled, findings exported to Security Hub). Missing/organizational: the remediation PROCESS itself (SLAs, triage, ticketing, ownership) and automated-remediation pipelines are process artifacts. The aging-findings controls are the closest config proxy for whether remediation is keeping up.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement processes, procedures, and technical measures to secure APIs. Review and update for any improvements at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.stave_controls_note: config_posture is the bulk; review-annually clause is organizational
controls.notes: Extensive config coverage of the CAIQ-named API security measures: authorization (route auth required, no sole-API-key auth, JWT audience/scope, Cognito scope, IAM resource restriction), API key/usage-plan management (quota, throttling, rate-based WAF), TLS/mTLS enforcement, WAF attachment, CORS hardening, private endpoints, response/credential exposure, and access logging. Mostly config_posture; marked partial only because the spec's 'review and update at least annually' clause is an organizational process that no snapshot can attest. Technical-measures portion is effectively full.

controls.aicm_specification: Validate, filter, modify or block, as necessary, input against adversarial patterns, failure patterns and unwanted behaviour according to organizational policies and applicable laws and regulations.
controls.stave_controls_note: config-verifiable input-validation enforcement at the infra/API layer
controls.notes: Config-verifiable slice (strong): API Gateway request validation against JSON schema (body/query/path/params, closed schemas, payload size caps, WebSocket message validation) plus WAF managed/OWASP rules in BLOCK mode and parser-limit protection — these enforce structural and known-adversarial-pattern input filtering at the infrastructure boundary. The Bedrock prompt-attack guardrail filter is a config flag covering AI-input adversarial filtering. Missing: application-layer/business-logic validation inside app code and true runtime semantic detection of novel adversarial/failure patterns are not snapshot-derivable. Marked partial: infra enforcement covered, in-app validation not.

controls.aicm_specification: Validate, filter, modify or block, as necessary, output against adversarial patterns, failure patterns and unwanted behaviour according to organisational policies and applicable laws and regulations.
controls.stave_controls_note: config-verifiable presence of output filtering mechanisms
controls.notes: Config-verifiable slice: presence of output-filtering mechanisms is checkable — Bedrock Guardrails sensitive-information (PII) filter and agent-must-have-guardrail confirm a GenAI output filter is attached; API Gateway response/server-header exposure controls strip internal detail from responses. Missing/runtime: the actual per-response validation of generated output against adversarial/failure patterns happens at inference time and is not a static config property. Stave can prove the filter is configured, not that it correctly blocks every bad output.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish security boundaries for agents.
controls.stave_controls_note: AI-Specific: these are CONFIG properties of the agent's IAM/network/guardrail boundary, not runtime behavior
controls.notes: AI-Specific. The security boundary of a (Bedrock) agent is largely config-verifiable: Stave scopes the agent execution role's lambda/model/S3 permissions (least-privilege blast radius), requires an attached guardrail, forbids public invocation endpoints, bounds idle session TTL, caps action-group sprawl, requires per-agent invocation logging, and flags dangling tool/KB references. These are static configuration of the agent's IAM/network/guardrail perimeter — NOT runtime tool-call interception. Missing: per-tool-call authorization decisions and dynamic boundary enforcement at execution time are runtime and out of snapshot scope; covered surface is AWS Bedrock-specific (no equivalent for other agent runtimes).

controls.aicm_specification: Implement source code management practices, such as version control, code review & static code analysis, aligning with the SDLC process.
controls.stave_controls_note: config_posture across GitHub + CodeCommit repo settings
controls.notes: Strong config coverage of SCM practices: version control + branch protection, code review enforcement (required approvals, CODEOWNERS, dismiss stale reviews, status checks, admin enforcement, no force push, linear history, signed commits), repo access control (org MFA, default permission scope, CodeCommit resource policy/approval rules), plus dependency and secret scanning. Marked partial rather than full because the 'static code analysis' aspect maps only to dependency/secret scanning here — actual SAST tool configuration/results are not a repo-config property, and only GitHub/CodeCommit providers are covered (no GitLab/Bitbucket equivalents).

controls.aicm_specification: Implement sandboxing techniques to execute AI tools and  plugins in isolated environments to prevent unintended  interactions with critical systems or data and limit the  possibility of lateral movement.
controls.stave_controls_note: AI-Specific: these are CONFIG properties approximating isolation (network isolation, VPC placement, no-internet, enclave), not a true sandbox/seccomp runtime boundary
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Stave has no control with a literal 'sandbox' property, but the isolation INTENT is partly config-verifiable: SageMaker model/training network isolation (no inbound/outbound), VPC-only placement for models/notebooks/training, notebook no-direct-internet, VPC-attached Lambda in private subnets, scoped agent tool-invocation permissions (limits lateral movement), Nitro Enclaves for cryptographic isolation, and prod/non-prod VPC isolation. These approximate 'isolated environment + limit lateral movement.' Missing/gap: no control models AI-tool/plugin execution sandboxing directly (e.g. container seccomp/gVisor/Firecracker microVM isolation flags, plugin egress allowlists). A purpose-built control SHOULD check the AI tool/plugin execution environment's isolation properties: network egress restriction, filesystem/credential scoping, and runtime sandbox flag (microVM/container isolation enabled).

controls.aicm_specification: Implement security measures to protect caches in GenAI systems and  services.
controls.stave_controls_note: AI-Specific: config-verifiable cache hardening on generic cache layers; no GenAI-cache-specific property
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Generic cache-protection properties that would back a GenAI cache are config-verifiable: API Gateway cache at-rest encryption and cache-key scoping (prevents cross-tenant cache key collisions), authorizer cache TTL bounding, CloudFront not caching authorized/per-user responses, and ElastiCache at-rest/in-transit encryption + AUTH token. Gap: no control models a GenAI-specific semantic/prompt-response cache (e.g. embedding cache, prompt cache) — its tenant-isolation, TTL, and PII-in-cache risks are not represented. A purpose-built control SHOULD check the GenAI cache layer: encryption, per-tenant cache-key partitioning, and exclusion of sensitive prompt/response content from shared caches.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement mechanisms enabling the model to clearly distinguish user-provided input instructions from data and system instructions (e.g., system prompts).
controls.notes: AI-Specific and fundamentally runtime/model-internal. Distinguishing user instructions from data vs system prompts is a property of prompt construction and model inference behavior (delimiter/role separation, instruction-hierarchy handling) evaluated at inference time — not a static cloud-config property. The nearest config proxy is CTL.BEDROCK.GUARDRAIL.PROMPTATTACK.001 (prompt-injection filter), but that is a separate mitigation, not the differentiation mechanism this control requires; mapping it here would overstate coverage. No config snapshot can attest the model demarcates instruction sources, so this is out_of_scope_runtime.

domains.domain: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience

controls.aicm_title: Business Continuity Management Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate  and maintain business continuity management and operational  resilience policies and procedures. Review and update the policies and procedures at least  annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure policy lifecycle requirement (establish/document/approve/communicate/review annually). No cloud-configuration property to evaluate from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Determine the impact of business disruptions and risks to establish criteria for developing business continuity and operational resilience  strategies and capabilities. Review and update the risk assessment and impact analysis at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Business impact analysis is an analytical/governance process performed by people; nothing in a config snapshot attests to it.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish strategies to reduce the impact of business disruptions, and improve resiliency and recovery from business disruptions.
controls.notes: Defining a resilience strategy is organizational. Technical realizations of a strategy (redundancy/backup) are evaluated by BCR-08/BCR-11; the strategy document itself is not config-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and  maintain a business continuity plan based on the results of the operational resilience strategies and capabilities.
controls.notes: Existence/maintenance of a written BC plan is a documentation/governance artifact, not a cloud resource property.

controls.aicm_specification: Develop, identify, and acquire documentation,  both internally and from external parties, that is relevant to support the business continuity and operational resilience plans. Make the documentation available to authorized stakeholders and review at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Documentation development, distribution, and annual review is a human process with no infrastructure configuration to assess.

controls.aicm_specification: Exercise and test business continuity and operational resilience plans at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Conducting BC test exercises is an operational activity. A snapshot cannot evidence that an exercise was run; backup-restore verification (the closest config proxy) is not represented by any Stave property.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and maintain communication channels with all relevant  stakeholders in the course of business continuity and resilience  procedures.
controls.notes: Stakeholder communication channels/contact processes are organizational; not a configuration property of cloud resources.

controls.aicm_specification: Periodically perform backups. Ensure the confidentiality, integrity  and availability of the backup, and verify restoration from backup for resiliency.
controls.notes: Strong config coverage for 'periodically perform backups' (backup plan exists, automated backups enabled per service, backups recent) and for backup CIA (encryption=confidentiality, vault lock + recovery-account isolation + soft-delete=integrity, multi-AZ/cross-region replication=availability). MISSING: the spec's restoration-verification clause ('verify restoration from backup for resiliency') is an operational test that no static snapshot or Stave control evidences. Hence partial, not full.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain a disaster response plan to recover from natural and man-made disasters. Update the plan at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Existence/maintenance of a DR plan document is governance. DR technical readiness (cross-region replication, multi-region KMS, ECR replication) is evaluated under BCR-08/BCR-11; the plan artifact itself is not config-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Exercise the disaster response plan annually or upon  significant changes, including, if possible, the participation  of local emergency authorities.
controls.notes: Running an annual DR exercise (with emergency authorities) is an operational/human activity with no configuration footprint a snapshot can capture.

controls.aicm_specification: Supplement business-critical equipment with both locally redundant and geographically dispersed equipment located at a reasonable minimum distance in accordance with applicable industry standards.
controls.notes: Cloud equivalent of 'locally redundant' = Multi-AZ / HA across services (covered broadly) and 'geographically dispersed at minimum distance' = cross-region replication / multi-region keys (covered for RDS, S3, backup vault, EKS DR, KMS). MISSING for full: no single control attests that ALL business-critical equipment is redundant (coverage is per-resource-type, gated on criticality tags), and 'reasonable minimum distance in accordance with industry standards' is not evaluated as a quantitative property. A would-be gap control: verify every criticality-tagged resource has a redundant replica in a region at/above a minimum geographic separation.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and  maintain policies and procedures for managing the risks  associated with applying changes to assets owned, controlled or  used by the organization. Review and update the policies and  procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance: establish/document/approve/communicate/review-annually change-management policy. No configuration artifact to evaluate from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, maintain and implement a defined quality change  control, approval and testing process incorporating baselines, testing, and release standards.
controls.notes: Describes a quality/approval/testing PROCESS incorporating baselines and release standards. The process itself is human/procedural and not verifiable from a config snapshot. The baseline artifact aspect is addressed separately under CCC-06.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement a change management procedure to manage the risks associated with applying changes to assets owned, controlled or used by the organization.
controls.notes: The procedure itself is organizational, but its technical enforcement IS config-verifiable. Stave confirms AWS Config is recording all resource types/regions (so changes are tracked) and that StackSet deployments require administrator approval. Missing: no control verifies a CI/CD change-management gating system (e.g. CodePipeline approval stages) exists.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement and enforce a procedure to authorize the addition, removal, update, and management of assets that are owned, controlled or used by the organization.
controls.notes: Strong config coverage for preventing/detecting unauthorized changes: out-of-band/console drift detection (OpenSearch, StepFunctions, CloudFormation), termination protection on stacks, restricting who can stop/delete the change-tracking machinery (Config recorder/rule access + SCP). Partial: detection is per-service and not exhaustive across all asset types; the authorization PROCEDURE (who approves an add/remove) remains organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Include provisions limiting changes directly impacting service customers owned environments (tenants) to explicitly authorized requests within service level agreements.
controls.notes: Contractual/SLA provisions limiting tenant-impacting changes to authorized requests. This lives in legal agreements and a request-authorization workflow, not in any cloud configuration property.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document and implement change management and configuration baselines for all relevant authorized changes on organization assets. Review and update the baselines at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: A configuration baseline in AWS terms is a deployed set of Config rules / conformance packs. Stave verifies that active Config rules exist, that conformance packs are deployed (account + org level) and that rules are not disabled — i.e. that a baseline is actually established and enforced. Partial: the 'establish/document/review annually' lifecycle governance is organizational and the baseline's substantive contents are out of scope here.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement detection measures with proactive notification in case of changes deviating from the established baseline.
controls.notes: Excellent config-posture coverage of deviation detection + proactive notification: Config rules must be evaluating (not ERROR/never-triggered), drift detection enabled (CloudFormation, OpenSearch console, StepFunctions), and notification plumbing present (delivery SNS topic, delivery-failure and conformance-score alarms, per-service config-change alarms). Partial only because notification coverage is service-specific rather than universal; the deviation-detection capability itself is verifiable from snapshot config.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement a procedure for the management of exceptions, including emergencies, in the change and configuration process. Align the procedure with the requirements of GRC-04: Policy Exception Process.
controls.notes: Exception/emergency-change PROCEDURE aligned to a policy-exception process (GRC-04). This is workflow/governance with no configuration property to evaluate from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement a process to proactively roll back changes to a previous known good state in case of errors or security concerns.
controls.notes: The rollback CAPABILITY is config-verifiable and Stave checks several aspects: CloudFormation stacks must have rollback enabled, ECS deployments must have circuit-breaker auto-rollback, IaC state must be versioned (enables restore to known-good). Partial: these are point checks per service; the org-wide 'define and implement a rollback process' remains procedural, and there is no general control verifying a tested restore/known-good-state mechanism exists for every asset class.

controls.aicm_title: Encryption and Key Management Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures for Cryptography, Encryption and Key Management.  Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance: establish/document/approve/communicate/review-annually a crypto policy. No configuration artifact to evaluate from a snapshot. The downstream technical enforcement of such a policy is captured by CEK-03/04/12 etc.; the policy lifecycle itself is a human process.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement cryptographic, encryption and key management roles and responsibilities.
controls.notes: Defining roles is organizational, but the technical enforcement of separation-of-duties for key management is config-verifiable. Stave checks key-admin vs key-user on the same principal (CTL.KMS.SEPARATION.001, GCP encrypter/decrypter separation), broad key-administration grants (CTL.KMS.POLICY.ADMIN.BROAD.001), and data-admin not holding key-deletion (CTL.BACKUP.RECOVERY.ISOLATION.002). Coverage is partial: the documentation/assignment of named roles is not snapshot-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Provide data protection at-rest, in-transit and, where applicable, in-use by using cryptographic libraries certified to approved standards.
controls.notes: Encryption-at-rest and in-transit are extensively covered across nearly every storage/data/transport service (S3, RDS, EBS, DynamoDB, EFS, Redshift, ElastiCache, OpenSearch, SNS/SQS, Kinesis, MSK, ELB/CloudFront/API Gateway TLS, plus Azure/GCP/vSphere equivalents) — the list above is representative, not exhaustive (147 *.ENCRYPT and 72 TLS/HTTPS controls exist). Partial, not full: (a) 'in-use' encryption (confidential computing / enclaves) is not checked; (b) 'cryptographic libraries certified to approved standards' (FIPS validation of the library) is only checked for KMS HSM origin (CTL.KMS.FIPS.001) and Redshift FIPS, not per-service.

controls.aicm_specification: Utilize encryption algorithms following industry standards for protecting data, based on the data classification and associated risks.
controls.notes: Algorithm/cipher strength is checked in many places: certificate key algorithms (ACM strong key algorithm, CloudFront/ELB weak-key RSA-1024, KeyVault RSA min size), TLS minimum versions and weak-cipher policies (ELB/API Gateway/CloudFront/RDS/OpenSearch/GCP SSL policy), weak VPN encryption, and DES-only Kerberos. Partial: no single control ties algorithm choice to a data-classification tag, and there is no generic 'symmetric encryption must use AES-256+' check for arbitrary at-rest services (most at-rest controls verify that encryption is on / CMK is used, not the cipher).

controls.aicm_specification: Establish a standard change management procedure, to accommodate changes from internal and external sources, for review, approval, implementation and communication of cryptographic, encryption and key management technology changes.
controls.notes: Change-management procedure (review/approve/implement/communicate crypto technology changes) is a process control. No snapshot property encodes the existence of a change-management workflow. Drift/state controls (e.g. KMS state, snapshot key drift) detect the effects of changes but not the procedure itself.

controls.aicm_specification: Manage and adopt changes to cryptography-, encryption-, and key management-related systems (including policies and procedures) that fully account for downstream effects of proposed changes, including residual risk, cost, and benefits analysis.
controls.notes: Requires a documented residual-risk/cost/benefit analysis accompanying crypto changes. Pure governance artifact; nothing in a configuration snapshot represents a cost-benefit analysis.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and maintain an encryption and key management risk program that includes provisions for risk assessment, risk treatment, risk context, monitoring, and feedback.
controls.notes: Establishing a risk-management program (assessment/treatment/monitoring/feedback loop) is organizational. Individual technical findings feed such a program but the program's existence and operation is not snapshot-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Service providers must provide the capability for service customers to manage their own data encryption keys.
controls.notes: Reframed for the customer side: Stave verifies that resources actually USE customer-managed keys (CMK/CMEK) rather than provider-owned/AWS-managed keys, across most services and all three clouds. This is the strongest evidence that customer key-management capability is being exercised. Partial because the AICM control is written from the service-PROVIDER obligation ('provide the capability'); a customer-posture snapshot cannot prove the provider offers the capability, only that the customer is using CMKs where available.

controls.aicm_specification: Audit encryption and key management systems, policies, and processes with a frequency that is proportional to the risk exposure of the system  with audit occurring preferably continuously but at least annually and after  any security event(s).
controls.notes: The 'audit at least annually / continuously' frequency and the audit program are organizational. But the technical preconditions for continuous auditing are config-verifiable: Stave checks that CloudTrail data events are enabled for Secrets Manager and that CloudWatch alarms exist for KMS policy changes, grant creation, deletion, disable, rotation failures, decrypt failures, and cross-account usage. Partial: presence of monitoring is checked; the audit cadence and review of findings is not.

controls.aicm_specification: Generate Cryptographic keys using industry accepted cryptographic libraries specifying the algorithm strength and the random number  generator used.
controls.notes: Key generation provenance/strength is partly verifiable: CTL.KMS.FIPS.001 requires keys originate from a FIPS 140-2 validated HSM (the industry-accepted-library + RNG assurance), KeyVault enforces minimum RSA key size, ACM enforces strong key algorithms. Partial/gap: a managed KMS key's generation already uses a vetted RNG inside the provider HSM, so the AICM emphasis on 'specifying the RNG' is largely satisfied by FIPS origin but not independently asserted. No control verifies the RNG type for imported/external key material beyond expiry presence.

controls.aicm_specification: Manage cryptographic secret and private keys that are provisioned for a unique purpose.
controls.notes: 'Unique purpose' / key scoping is well captured: CTL.KMS.CONCENTRATION.001 (one key must not encrypt >50 resources), CTL.KMS.ISOLATION.001 (PHI/CDE key must not be shared across sensitivity domains), CTL.KMS.LIFECYCLE.CROSSENV.001 (key not used across prod and non-prod), and policy scoping via ViaService/encryption-context restrictions. Partial: these enforce non-sharing/scoping heuristics rather than an explicit declared single-purpose attribute per key.

controls.aicm_specification: Rotate cryptographic keys in accordance with the calculated cryptoperiod, which includes provisions for considering the risk of information disclosure and legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: Strong, near-complete coverage: KMS CMK automatic rotation must be enabled (CTL.KMS.ROTATION.001), rotation period must not exceed compliance threshold / cryptoperiod (CTL.KMS.LIFECYCLE.ROTATION.PERIOD.001, CTL.SECRETS.ROTATION.INTERVAL.LONG.001), rotation-failure alarms, plus GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, Azure Storage account key, Step Functions key, Secrets Manager, access keys and SAML cert rotation. Full: the AICM cryptoperiod intent (rotate within a calculated/compliant interval) is directly enforced by the rotation-period controls. The 'calculated cryptoperiod' rationale is organizational but the enforced interval is config-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to revoke and remove cryptographic keys prior to the end of its established cryptoperiod, when a key is compromised, or an entity is no longer part of the organization, which include provisions for legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: Revocation when an entity leaves the org is config-verifiable as stale grants/policy references: orphaned KMS grants (deleted principal), key policies referencing deleted principals, keys granting access to decommissioned accounts, GCP/KeyVault bindings to deleted members, dangling KMS key references in IAM policies. Partial: Stave detects un-revoked access (the negative evidence) but does not model an active revocation workflow or revoke-before-cryptoperiod-end timing; the procedural definition is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures to securely destroy cryptographic keys when they are no longer needed, which include provisions for legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: Secure-destruction safeguards are config-verifiable: keys pending deletion while still referenced by active resources (CTL.KMS.STATE.PENDINGDELETION.001, CTL.KMS.PENDING.DELETION.001), minimum deletion waiting period as a safety window (CTL.KMS.DELETION.MINWAIT.001), high-density keys must have deletion protection (CTL.KMS.CONCENTRATION.002), Secrets Manager minimum recovery window and deletion-while-referenced. Partial: Stave guards AGAINST premature/unsafe destruction; it does not affirmatively verify that no-longer-needed keys ARE destroyed (that side is captured by dormant-key detection, CEK-17). The destruction process definition is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to create keys in a pre-activated state when they have been generated but not authorized for use, which include provisions for legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: The pre-activation state maps closest to KMS Origin=EXTERNAL keys awaiting material import: CTL.KMS.STATE.PENDINGIMPORT.001 fires when a key exists but has no material (operationally pre-active). Partial: this control treats pending-import as a defect (no material) rather than affirming a deliberate pre-activated-then-authorized workflow. Gap: no control verifies an intended 'created-but-not-yet-authorized' staging discipline; KMS has no first-class pre-activation state beyond pending-import/disabled.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to monitor, review and approve key transitions from any  state to/from suspension, which include provisions for legal and regulatory  requirements.
controls.notes: Suspension maps to the KMS Disabled state (reversible, no crypto ops). CTL.KMS.STATE.DISABLED.001 detects a key disabled while active resources still depend on it; CTL.KMS.ALARM.DISABLE.001 requires a CloudWatch alarm on DisableKey (the 'monitor transitions to/from suspension' intent). Partial: monitoring of the disable transition is covered; the review/approve workflow for the transition is organizational and not snapshot-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to deactivate keys at the time of their expiration date, which  include provisions for legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: Deactivation-at-expiration is config-verifiable: imported KMS key material without an expiration (CTL.KMS.IMPORTED.EXPIRY.001), expired KMS material still present (CTL.KMS.MATERIAL.EXPIRED.001), Key Vault keys/secrets without expiry dates, and dormant keys unused 90+ days while policy still grants access (CTL.KMS.LIFECYCLE.DORMANT.001 — effectively un-deactivated stale keys). Partial: Stave detects missing-expiry and past-due/unused keys; it does not model an automated deactivate-on-expiry action.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to manage archived keys in a secure repository requiring least  privilege access, which include provisions for legal and regulatory  requirements.
controls.notes: 'Secure repository with least-privilege access' maps to key-policy least-privilege controls: KMS policy must restrict to specific roles (CTL.KMS.POLICY.001), no broad admin/decrypt/cross-account, and the Key Vault is the explicit archival repository (soft-delete/purge protection, RBAC instead of access policies, no public network). Dormant-key policy minimization covers archived-but-still-granting keys. Partial: there is no first-class 'archived key' state in KMS; controls enforce least-privilege on keys generally, not a dedicated archival repository lifecycle.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to use compromised keys to encrypt information only in  controlled circumstance, and thereafter exclusively for decrypting data  and never for encrypting data, which include provisions for legal and  regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: The core requirement — restricting a compromised key to decrypt-only and never encrypt — has no direct KMS configuration analog (KMS key usage is encrypt+decrypt as a unit; you cannot config a key to decrypt-only). That handling discipline is organizational/runtime. Partial/weak: the closest config support is monitoring for anomalous/compromise-indicative usage (cross-account alarms, decrypt-volume/failure alarms) and restricting decrypt principals. Gap: a control asserting a flagged-compromised key is disabled for new encrypt operations would require a compromise-status property that does not exist; nearest practical action is CTL.KMS.STATE.DISABLED.001 / scheduled re-key.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to assess the risk to operational continuity versus the risk of  the keying material and the information it protects being exposed if  control of the keying material is lost, which include provisions for legal  and regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: The continuity-vs-exposure assessment is organizational, but its technical measures are config-verifiable: multi-region key replication for recoverability (CTL.KMS.MULTIREGION.NOREPLICA.001 and related), Key Vault soft-delete/purge protection (recoverable repository), backup-key account isolation (recovery without single-account loss), and deletion waiting period. Partial: Stave verifies the recoverability controls exist; the risk trade-off analysis itself is not snapshot-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures in order for the key management system to track and report  all cryptographic materials and changes in status, which include provisions  for legal and regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: Inventory hygiene and status tracking are config-verifiable: every key should have an alias for inventory (CTL.KMS.LIFECYCLE.NOALIAS.001), aliases must not be orphaned/ghost-pointing (inventory integrity), and key states (disabled, pending-deletion, pending-import, dormant) are all surfaced as findings — i.e. Stave evaluates the full key state inventory each snapshot and reports status. Change-in-status reporting is supported via alarm controls (policy change, rotation events). Partial: Stave reports per-key status but does not itself constitute the authoritative KMS inventory/reporting system the AICM control mandates; it audits the inventory rather than maintaining it.

controls.aicm_title: Physical and Environmental Security Policy and Procedures

controls.notes: Establish/document/review physical & environmental security policy. Pure physical/environmental security policy-and-procedure control. No cloud-configuration artifact is observable from a tenant infrastructure snapshot; in the shared-responsibility model the physical datacenter is the CSP's responsibility and inherited by the tenant. Out of Stave's scope.

controls.notes: Off-site equipment disposal / media destruction policy. Physical equipment lifecycle process; no infrastructure-snapshot property. controls.notes: Off-site hardware/software/data transfer authorization process. Organizational approval workflow; not a configuration property. controls.aicm_title: Secure Media Transportation Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures for the secure transportation of physical media. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Secure physical-media transportation policy. Pure physical/environmental security policy-and-procedure control. No cloud-configuration artifact is observable from a tenant infrastructure snapshot; in the shared-responsibility model the physical datacenter is the CSP's responsibility and inherited by the tenant. controls.aicm_specification: Classify and document the physical, and logical assets (e.g., applications) based on the organizational business risk. Review and update the assets’ classification at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Asset classification covers physical AND logical assets. The physical-asset classification and the documented, annually-reviewed classification program are organizational and out of scope. Stave can partially verify the logical-asset side: it checks that resources carry data-classification / compliance tags or labels (EKS namespace data-classification label, EventBridge data-classification tags, Cognito compliance tags). These verify the *artifact* of a classification scheme on specific resource types, not a comprehensive program. Missing: a generic cross-service 'all critical resources must carry an approved data-classification tag' control, plus the documented program and annual-review cadence (inherently organizational).

controls.aicm_specification: Catalogue and track all relevant physical and logical assets located at all of the service provider's sites within a secured system. Review and update the catalogue at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Catalogue and track physical AND logical assets in a secured system. Physical-asset cataloguing and the secured catalogue system / annual review are organizational. Logical-asset tracking has a config angle Stave partially covers: S3 Inventory enablement for object visibility, restricting SSM Inventory access, and shadow/unmanaged-resource detection (e.g. OpenSearch cross-cluster connection not in inventory). These are point checks, not a unified asset-catalogue assertion. Missing: a control verifying a complete, authoritative resource inventory (e.g. AWS Config recorder enabled across all resource types / regions) and tag-completeness across the estate; the catalogue program itself is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Design and implement physical security perimeters to safeguard personnel, data, and information systems.
controls.notes: Design/implement physical security perimeters. Physical (Phys-only arch relevance). Pure physical/environmental security policy-and-procedure control. The 'technical measures' aspect is strongly config-verifiable and Stave covers it well at the tenant resource level: critical resources have backups (BACKUP.EXISTS / PLAN.EXISTS), backups are recent (BACKUP.RECENT), resources span multiple AZs (BACKUP.MULTIAZ, AUTOSCALING.MULTIAZ), and critical data is cross-region replicated (BACKUP.REPLICATION). domains.domain: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management

controls.aicm_title: Security and Privacy Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate,  apply, evaluate and maintain policies and  procedures for the preparation, classification,  protection and handling of data throughout  its lifecycle, and according to all applicable  laws and regulations, standards, and risk level.  Review and update the policies and  procedures at least annually, or upon  significant changes.
controls.notes: Establish/document/approve/communicate/review data lifecycle policies annually. Pure governance process; no config artifact in a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Apply industry accepted methods for the secure disposal of data from storage media such that data is not recoverable by any forensic means.
controls.notes: Secure disposal so data is non-recoverable. Stave can verify crypto-erase prerequisites and deletion safeguards (KMS key-deletion separation of duties, soft-delete/purge-protection settings) but cannot attest forensic non-recoverability of media (DoD/NIST wipe), which is the core requirement. Cloud disposal is largely provider-managed; key destruction (crypto-shredding) is the verifiable proxy. Missing: a control asserting CMK-backed encryption + key-destruction lifecycle as the disposal mechanism for a bucket/volume.

controls.aicm_specification: Create and maintain a data inventory, at least for any sensitive, regulated  and personal data. Review and update the inventory at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Maintain a data inventory for sensitive/regulated/personal data. Stave checks that storage resources carry a data-classification tag (presence of inventory metadata) but does not maintain or validate an enterprise inventory register or its annual review. Tag-coverage is a partial proxy for inventory completeness.

controls.aicm_specification: Classify data according to its type, criticality and sensitivity level.
controls.notes: Classify data by type/criticality/sensitivity. Stave verifies that resources carry data-classification tags/labels (S3 buckets, EventBridge buses, EKS namespaces) but cannot verify the classification value is correct vs the actual data content; presence-of-tag only. Coverage is partial across resource types (S3, EventBridge, EKS) and absent for many services (RDS, DynamoDB, EFS, etc.).

controls.aicm_specification: Create data flow documentation to identify what data is processed, stored or transmitted where. Review data flow documentation at defined intervals, at least annually, and upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Create/maintain data flow documentation (what data processed/stored/transmitted where) reviewed annually. Documentation artifact and process; network topology can be observed but the required deliverable is documentation, not config.

controls.aicm_specification: Document ownership and stewardship of all relevant documented personal and sensitive data. Perform review at least annually.
controls.notes: Document ownership/stewardship of personal & sensitive data with annual review. Pure governance role-assignment process; no config artifact (arch relevance empty in AICM).

controls.aicm_title: Data Protection by Design and Default
controls.aicm_specification: Develop systems, products, and business practices based upon a principle of security by design and industry best practices.
controls.notes: Security-by-design as a business-practice principle. The abstract principle is organizational, but Stave's entire catalog (encryption-at-rest/in-transit, PAB, least-privilege, segmentation) is the technical embodiment of secure defaults. Listed controls are representative; the AICM control itself is a broad principle so coverage is inherently partial - no single control satisfies it.

controls.aicm_title: Data Privacy by Design and Default
controls.aicm_specification: Develop systems, products, and business practices based upon a principle of privacy by design and industry best practices. Ensure that systems' privacy settings are configured by default, according to all applicable laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Privacy-by-default: privacy settings configured by default. Stave can verify restrictive defaults (block public access, PII filters, no public sensitive data) which embody privacy-protective defaults, but the legal/regulatory privacy-program aspect is organizational. Partial: config-default proxies exist, full privacy-by-design is not snapshot-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) to evaluate the origin, nature, particularity and severity of the risks upon the processing of personal data, according to any applicable laws, regulations and industry best practices.
controls.notes: Conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA). Assessment process/document; no config artifact.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures that ensure any transfer of personal or sensitive data is protected from unauthorized access and only processed within scope as permitted by the respective laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Transfer of personal/sensitive data protected from unauthorized access and processed only within permitted scope. Config-verifiable: in-transit encryption (TLS) enforcement broadly covered, plus jurisdictional access scoping (SOVEREIGNTY). Partial: 'only processed within scope permitted by laws' (purpose/legal scoping) is organizational and not fully covered.

controls.aicm_title: Personal Data Access, Reversal, Rectification and Deletion
controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement, processes, procedures and technical measures to enable data subjects to request access to, modification, or deletion of their personal data, according to any applicable laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Enable data-subject access/rectification/deletion (DSAR) requests. Application-level capability and process; not a cloud-config property in a snapshot.

controls.aicm_title: Limitation of Purpose in Personal Data Processing
controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to ensure that personal data is processed according to any applicable laws and regulations and for the purposes declared to the data subject.
controls.notes: Purpose limitation: personal data processed only for declared purposes per law. Legal/process control over data usage intent; not config-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures for the transfer and sub-processing of personal data within the service supply chain, according to any applicable laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Sub-processing of personal data within the supply chain per law. Contractual/process control over sub-processors; not config-verifiable. (Cross-account access controls touch adjacent territory but the requirement is legal sub-processing governance.)

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to disclose the details of any personal or sensitive data access by sub-processors to the data owner prior to initiation of that processing.
controls.notes: Disclose sub-processor data-access details to the data owner before processing. Disclosure/notification process; no config artifact.

controls.aicm_specification: Obtain authorization from data owners, and manage associated risk before replicating or using production data in non-production environments.
controls.notes: Obtain authorization and manage risk before replicating/using production data in non-production. The authorization step is organizational. Config-adjacent: detecting non-prod-to-prod routing/cross-env coupling. No Stave control detects copying of production data into a non-prod environment. Missing: a control flagging prod data classification tags on resources in non-prod accounts/environments.

controls.aicm_specification: Data retention, archiving and deletion is managed in accordance with business requirements, applicable laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Retention/archiving/deletion managed per business/legal requirements. Strongly config-verifiable: retention policies, object-lock/immutability, lifecycle rules, backup retention floors. Partial only because the per-dataset legal retention requirement must be supplied as policy; Stave verifies a configured retention/lock exists and meets a floor but not that the value matches the governing law for that specific data.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement, processes, procedures and technical measures to protect sensitive data throughout its lifecycle.
controls.notes: Protect sensitive data throughout its lifecycle. Broad config coverage: KMS encryption of sensitive buckets, no public sensitive data, Macie discovery, exposure/exfil reachability, VPC isolation for sensitive workloads. Partial: 'throughout lifecycle' includes process stages (creation/disposal) that go beyond static config.

controls.aicm_specification: The service providers must implement and describe to service customers the procedure to manage and respond to requests for disclosure of Personal Data by Law Enforcement Authorities according to applicable laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Procedure to handle Law-Enforcement disclosure requests for personal data. Pure process/notification control.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement, processes, procedures and technical measures to specify and document the physical locations of data, including any locations in which data is processed or backed up.
controls.notes: Specify/document physical locations where data is stored, processed, backed up. Config-verifiable residency: region-restriction SCPs/conditions, resources in unauthorized regions, sovereignty reachability, multi-region key placement, snapshot/backup region. Partial: the documentation deliverable and physical-location attestation are organizational; Stave verifies the enforced region constraints which is the technical core.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to:  1) Document and trace data sources, and 2) Make the data source available according to legal and regulatory requirements
controls.notes: Document/trace data sources (provenance) and make source available per law. Mostly organizational (lineage documentation). Config-adjacent: Stave can identify which data sources feed AI knowledge bases / training jobs (source bucket bindings, cross-account source boundaries), giving partial provenance visibility. No dedicated data-lineage/provenance-record control. Missing: a control asserting recorded source-of-record metadata for datasets.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to prevent data poisoning in AI models and continuously detect such.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Prevent AND continuously detect data poisoning in AI models. CONFIG aspect (prevention): Stave verifies training/KB data-source integrity prerequisites - source must not cross account boundaries, must be encrypted reads, S3 access scoped to declared sources - which harden the pipeline against unauthorized data injection. RUNTIME aspect (continuous detection): poisoning detection during/after training requires behavioral monitoring/statistical anomaly checks - out of scope for a static snapshot. Partial: prevention hardening covered, detection is runtime-only.

controls.aicm_specification: Use Privacy Enhancing Technologies for training data, informed by risk and privacy impact analysis and business use cases.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Use Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETs) for training data (differential privacy, federated learning, encryption, anonymization). CONFIG: Stave can verify training data is encrypted and that Bedrock guardrails enable a PII/sensitive-information filter (a deployable PET-adjacent control). It cannot verify differential privacy, k-anonymity, or pseudonymization applied to dataset content - those are dataset-content/algorithm properties not in a config snapshot. Largely a gap. Missing: control asserting an anonymization/DP transform is configured in the training pipeline.

controls.aicm_specification: Regularly validate the consistency and conformity of training, fine-tuning or augmentation data. Implement dataset versioning to ensure traceability and enforce restrictions to prevent unauthorized changes.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Validate consistency/conformity of training/fine-tuning/augmentation data; implement dataset versioning for traceability; enforce restrictions against unauthorized changes. CONFIG: dataset versioning (S3/GCS object versioning), immutability (object lock), and write-access restriction (scoped S3 roles, no cross-account source) are verifiable proxies for traceability + unauthorized-change prevention. RUNTIME: 'regularly validate consistency/conformity' is a data-quality validation job, behavioral/process - not config. Partial: versioning + access-restriction covered; consistency validation is runtime/process.

controls.aicm_specification: Ensure training-data differentiation and relevance to the intended use of the AI Model.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Ensure training-data differentiation and relevance to the AI model's intended use. This is a data-quality/data-curation property of dataset content (is the data relevant and properly differentiated for the use case) - assessed by analyzing the dataset and model purpose, not derivable from any cloud-config snapshot. No config artifact.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate  and maintain policies and procedures for an information  governance program, which is sponsored by the leadership  of the organization and related to AI systems as well.  Review and update the policies and procedures at least  annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance program: establish/document/approve/communicate/maintain policies, review annually. No config artifact in a cloud snapshot; org process only.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and maintain a formal, documented, and leadership-sponsored AI Risk Management (AIRM) program that includes policies and  procedures for identification, evaluation, ownership, treatment, and acceptance of risks.
controls.notes: Formal documented AI Risk Management program with policies/procedures for risk identification, ownership, treatment, acceptance. Organizational program, not config-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Review all relevant organizational policies and associated procedures at least annually or when a substantial change occurs within the organization.
controls.notes: Annual review of organizational policies. Pure cadence/process control; no snapshot evidence.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and follow an approved exception process as mandated by the governance program whenever a deviation from an established policy occurs.
controls.notes: Approved exception process for policy deviations. Workflow/governance process; not represented in cloud config.

controls.aicm_specification: Develop and implement an Information Security Program, which includes programs for all the relevant domains of the AICM.
controls.notes: Develop/implement an Information Security Program spanning all AICM domains. Program-level governance, organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and document roles and responsibilities for planning, implementing, operating, assessing, and improving governance programs.
controls.notes: Define/document governance roles and responsibilities (RACI). Org documentation, not config. Note: IAM role *assignments* are config-verifiable but this control is about governance accountability documentation, not IAM grants.

controls.aicm_specification: Identify and document all relevant standards, regulations,  legal/contractual, and statutory requirements, which are  applicable to your organization.  Review at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Identify/document applicable standards/regulations/legal requirements; annual review. Regulatory mapping is documentation; not a config snapshot property.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and maintain contact with related special interest groups and other relevant entities in line with business context.
controls.notes: Maintain contact with special interest groups. Purely organizational relationship-management.

controls.aicm_title: Acceptable Use of the AI Service
controls.aicm_specification: Define, document and enforce policies and procedures on the acceptable use of AI services offered by the organization. Ensure effectiveness by continuous risk assessments, reviews and human oversight.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Define/document/enforce acceptable-use policies for AI services with continuous risk assessment and human oversight. The policy and oversight aspects are organizational; 'enforce' could in principle map to IAM/guardrail config (e.g. Bedrock guardrails, IAM allow/deny on model invocation) but the control's intent is policy governance + behavioral oversight, not a static config property. No Stave control verifies acceptable-use policy.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, and communicate to all relevant stakeholders an AI Impact Assessment process and its criteria to regularly evaluate the ethical, societal, operational, legal, and security impacts of the AI system throughout its lifecycle.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Establish/document an AI Impact Assessment process evaluating ethical/societal/legal/operational/security impacts across lifecycle. Process/documentation; runtime+organizational, not config.

controls.aicm_specification: Regularly evaluate AI systems, models, datasets & algorithms for bias and fairness to ensure compliance with ethical standards.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Evaluate models/datasets/algorithms for bias and fairness. Requires running evaluations against model outputs/datasets (behavioral/runtime) plus organizational ethics standards. Not derivable from a config snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish an ethics committee to review AI applications, ensuring alignment with ethical standards and organizational values.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Establish an ethics committee. Purely organizational body.

controls.aicm_specification: Evaluate, document, and communicate the degree of explainability of the AI Services, including possible limitations and exceptions.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Evaluate/document/communicate achieved explainability incl. limitations. Requires assessing model behavior (runtime) plus documentation; not a static config property.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, execute, and assess processes, procedures, and technical measures to ensure human oversight and control of the AI system in compliance with regulatory requirements and organizational risk management.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Establish/execute/assess human oversight and control processes for the AI system. Primarily organizational process; the 'technical measures' clause could in theory include config (e.g. approval gates, IAM separation, kill-switch) but the control's verifiable subject is the oversight process and live human-in-the-loop behavior (runtime), not a snapshot property. No Stave control checks human-oversight configuration.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate  and maintain policies and procedures for background  verification of all new employees (including but not limited  to remote employees, contractors, and third parties)  according to local laws, regulations, ethics, and contractual  constraints and proportional to the data classification to be  accessed, the business requirements, and acceptable risk.  Review and update the policies and procedures at least  annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Background verification of new hires/contractors per local law and data classification. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.
