controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate  and maintain policies and procedures for defining  allowances and conditions for the acceptable use of  organizationally-owned or managed assets. Review and  update the policies and procedures at least annually,  or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Acceptable-use policy for org-owned/managed assets. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate  and maintain policies and procedures that require  unattended workspaces to not have openly visible  confidential data.  Review and update the policies and procedures at least  annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Clean-desk policy: unattended workspaces must not expose confidential data. Physical/behavioral. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_title: Remote and Home Working Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate  and maintain policies and procedures to protect information  accessed, processed or stored at remote sites and locations.  Review and update the policies and procedures at least  annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Remote/home-working policy to protect information at remote sites. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and document procedures for the return of  organization-owned assets by terminated employees,  contractors and third parties.
controls.notes: Procedures for return of org-owned assets by terminated employees/contractors. Pure HR process control. Establish/document/communicate procedures — no technical config component. The access-revocation OUTCOME of offboarding has a config-verifiable proxy in Stave (CTL.IAM.ACCOUNT.INACTIVE.001 'Inactive Accounts Must Be Disabled', CTL.IAM.CRED.UNUSED.001 'Disable Unused Credentials', CTL.AD.ACCOUNT.STALE.001), which detect lingering active credentials for departed users — but these verify staleness, not the HR termination/asset-return workflow itself. The control as specified is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, and communicate to all relevant  personnel the procedures outlining the roles and  responsibilities concerning changes in employment.
controls.notes: Procedures and roles/responsibilities for employment changes (including termination). Pure HR process control. Establish/document/communicate procedures — no technical config component. The access-revocation OUTCOME of offboarding has a config-verifiable proxy in Stave (CTL.IAM.ACCOUNT.INACTIVE.001 'Inactive Accounts Must Be Disabled', CTL.IAM.CRED.UNUSED.001 'Disable Unused Credentials', CTL.AD.ACCOUNT.STALE.001), which detect lingering active credentials for departed users — but these verify staleness, not the HR termination/asset-return workflow itself. The control as specified is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Employees sign the employee agreement prior to being granted access to organizational information systems, resources and assets.
controls.notes: Employees sign employment agreement before access is granted. Procedural gate, no config artifact. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: The organization includes within the employment agreements provisions and/or terms for adherence to established information governance and security policies.
controls.notes: Employment agreements must include adherence to infosec/governance policies. Contract content. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document and communicate  roles and responsibilities of employees, as  they relate to information assets' security  and privacy.
controls.notes: Establish/document/communicate personnel security & privacy roles and responsibilities. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Identify, document, and review, at planned intervals, requirements for non-disclosure/confidentiality agreements reflecting the organization's needs for the protection of data and operational details.
controls.notes: Identify/review NDA / confidentiality agreement requirements. Contractual/legal. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain a security awareness training program for all employees of the organization and provide regular training updates.
controls.notes: Security awareness training program for all employees with regular updates. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_title: Personal and Sensitive Data Awareness and Training
controls.aicm_specification: Provide employees with access to sensitive organizational and personal data with appropriate security awareness training and regular  updates in organizational procedures, processes, and policies relating  to their professional function relative to the organization.
controls.notes: Security awareness training for personnel with access to sensitive/personal data. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Make employees aware of their roles and responsibilities for maintaining awareness and compliance with established policies and procedures and applicable legal, statutory, or regulatory compliance obligations.
controls.notes: Make employees aware of compliance roles/responsibilities and legal/regulatory obligations. Organizational HR policy/procedure control: establish, document, approve, communicate, and review policies. No cloud-configuration component verifiable from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures defining the AI training program for all relevant personnel of the organization based on their roles and provide regular training updates.
controls.notes: AI-Specific: AI competency training program for relevant personnel by role. Despite AI-Specific tag, this is a training/policy control with no config or runtime property — no Stave bedrock/sagemaker/iam surface verifies whether staff completed AI training. Purely organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, and communicate to all personnel the policies and procedures on the acceptable use of AI technologies within the organization.
controls.notes: AI-Specific: acceptable-use policy for AI technologies. AI-Specific tag, but the control is establishing/communicating an acceptable-use POLICY — organizational, not config/runtime. (Technical enforcement of AI usage, e.g. restricting Bedrock model invocation, would be a separate config control; this control as written governs the policy document, not its technical enforcement.)

controls.aicm_title: Identity and Access Management Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, implement, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures for identity and access management. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: 'Establish, document, approve, communicate ... review at least annually' is pure governance/policy lifecycle for IAM. No technical configuration to verify from a snapshot. Stave enforces concrete IAM hygiene (MFA, least privilege, rotation) which implements such a policy, but the AICM control is the policy-document obligation itself.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, implement,  apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures for the  management of authentication credentials, including  passwords.  Review and update the policies and procedures at least  annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Credential-management POLICY-and-procedure obligation (document, approve, communicate, review annually). The technical realization is covered by IAM-14; this -02 control is the governance artifact, no config component.

controls.aicm_specification: Manage, store, and regularly review the inventory of identities, and monitor their level of access.
controls.notes: Inventory of identities + monitoring their access. Stave can verify config-observable aspects from a snapshot: enumerate IAM users/roles, flag inactive/stale/unused identities and credentials, and detect ghost/deleted principals still referenced in role assignments and resource policies. Missing: the organizational obligation to MAINTAIN and REGULARLY REVIEW the inventory as a process (review cadence/sign-off) is human process, not config.

controls.aicm_specification: Employ the separation of duties principle when implementing information system access.
controls.notes: Separation of duties when implementing system access. Stave verifies specific SoD-violating combinations from policy snapshots: encrypter+decrypter on one principal, key admin+user on one principal, SA admin+user on one principal, read+write to a secret by one principal, multi-step privilege-escalation paths, and data-admin holding KMS delete. Partial: there is no general engine that takes an arbitrary org-defined SoD matrix (e.g. requester vs approver, dev vs prod-deploy) and proves no single identity holds both halves; coverage is a fixed set of known toxic pairs.

controls.aicm_specification: Employ the least privilege principle when implementing information system access.
controls.notes: Least privilege is one of Stave's deepest surfaces. From an IAM-policy snapshot it detects full-admin grants, action/resource/service wildcards, net-effective admin-equivalent permissions, blast-radius to sensitive resources, permission drift, and per-service over-broad execution roles (EC2/ECS/Lambda/SageMaker/Bedrock/CodeBuild) across AWS, Azure RBAC, GCP and K8s RBAC. Marked full for the config-verifiable intent: 'employ least privilege when implementing access' is exactly attached-policy posture, which Stave proves comprehensively.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement an identity access provisioning process which  authorizes, records, and communicates access changes to data and assets.
controls.notes: 'Define and implement an identity access PROVISIONING PROCESS which authorizes, records, and communicates access changes.' This is a workflow/ticketing/approval process (who requested, who approved, recorded change). A static config snapshot shows the resulting state, not the provisioning workflow or its records/communications. No config property captures the process itself.

controls.aicm_specification: De-provision or modify identity access in a timely manner.
controls.notes: De-provision or modify access in a timely manner. Stave detects the config-observable failure mode of late de-provisioning: inactive accounts still enabled, unused credentials/roles not disabled, stale/ghost principals and IdPs still referenced in role assignments/trust/resource policies. Missing: timeliness relative to an HR de-provisioning event (the 'in a timely manner' SLA tied to a leaver) is process-bound and not derivable from infra config alone.

controls.aicm_specification: Review and revalidate identity access for least privilege and  separation of duties with a frequency that is commensurated  with organizational risk tolerance and at least annually, or  upon significant changes.
controls.notes: 'Review and revalidate identity access for least privilege and SoD ... at least annually.' Stave can produce the technical evidence a reviewer needs (current least-privilege violations, permission drift, unused grants, SoD pairs) on every snapshot, effectively continuous revalidation of the posture. Missing: the periodic-review GOVERNANCE event (attestation, sign-off, annual cadence) is organizational and not a config property.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures for the segregation of privileged access roles.
controls.notes: Segregation of privileged access roles. Stave verifies privileged-role segregation in config: admin perm-sets isolated, PIM/conditional-access required for privileged roles, privileged-role scope not at subscription level, admin/owner not broadly assigned, privileged-group membership bounded and non-nested, and toxic privileged combinations (KMS admin+user). Partial: it checks that privileged roles ARE segregated/restricted, but cannot prove the org's full intended segregation model for every custom privileged role pairing.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement an access process to ensure privileged access roles and rights are granted for a time limited period, and implement procedures to prevent the accumulation of segregated privileged access.
controls.notes: Privileged access granted for a TIME-LIMITED period + prevent accumulation of segregated privileged access. Time-bounding is config-verifiable: max session duration <=4h, federated session limits, short-lived credentials, credential expiry/TTL, Azure PIM (just-in-time). Accumulation is partly covered by permission-drift detection. Missing/partial: PIM-style just-in-time elevation for AWS native roles and an explicit 'no standing privileged access' check are only partially modeled; Azure PIM is the closest direct match.

controls.aicm_title: Service Customers' Approval for Agreed Privileged Access Roles
controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes and procedures  for service customers to participate, where applicable, in  the granting of access for agreed, high risk (as defined by  the organizational risk assessment) privileged access roles.
controls.notes: Service customers participate in granting high-risk privileged access (customer approval / vendor access controls). Mostly an approval-workflow obligation (organizational). Config-verifiable slivers Stave covers: customer can revoke a vendor's S3 access, vendor role is not over-privileged, delegated-admin scope, third-party trust scoping. Missing: the customer-approval gating workflow for granting the role is process, not config.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures, that ensure identities’ activities are identifiable through uniquely associated IDs.
controls.notes: Activities identifiable through uniquely associated IDs. Config-verifiable aspects Stave covers well: discourage shared/default service principals (per-instance/per-service/per-function roles, no shared task/lambda/studio roles, no default service accounts, no shared mailbox sign-in), require RoleSessionName/SourceIdentity so federated actions trace to an individual, and discourage root/shared-account daily use. Partial: it cannot prove every human has a distinct named identity (no shared logins) account-wide — it catches the common shared-credential anti-patterns, not a complete uniqueness guarantee.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures for authenticating access to systems, application and data assets, including multifactor authentication for at least privileged user and sensitive data access. Adopt digital certificates or alternatives which achieve an equivalent level of security for system identities.
controls.notes: Strong authentication incl. MFA for privileged/sensitive access and digital certificates for system identities. Deep config coverage: MFA enforced for console users, root (hardware), SSO, cross-cloud, and on destructive actions; weak/SMS-only MFA flagged; phishing-resistant MFA for admins; certificate-based auth for service principals and VPN (vs PSK). Marked full for the config-verifiable MFA/certificate intent across major providers.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures for the secure management of authentication credentials, including passwords.
controls.notes: Technical credential management incl. passwords. Stave comprehensively verifies password policy (length/complexity/expiration/reuse/rotation), access-key rotation/single-key/no-setup-key/no-root-key, automatic secret rotation and encryption, managed credentials via Secrets Manager/SSM, no plaintext credentials in env/userdata, and AD password policy. Full for the config-verifiable technical-measures intent (the policy-document side of credentials is IAM-02).

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to verify access to data and system functions is authorized.
controls.notes: Verify access to data and system functions is authorized (authorization mechanisms exist and are enforced). Config-verifiable: API routes require authorizers, IAM/JWT/Cognito authorizers properly scoped, K8s API server uses RBAC (not AlwaysAllow), data-layer resource policies deny unauthenticated/public/wildcard access. Partial because it spans the whole authorization surface; Stave verifies that authorization is configured and not bypassed on the surfaces it models, but 'all data and functions' is broader than any fixed control set.

controls.aicm_title: Knowledge Access Control - Need to Know
controls.aicm_specification: Define policy and procedure for "need to know" access to knowledge, information and data within the organization and in the context of the AI system to be applied when regulating access to resources.
controls.notes: Need-to-know access to knowledge/information/data, including in the AI-system context. Config-verifiable enforcement Stave covers: tenant/prefix isolation, encryption-key isolation across sensitivity domains, roles not reaching PHI-tagged buckets, AI knowledge-base/training-data roles scoped to their own data sources and not crossing account boundaries. Partial: the data-classification + need-to-know POLICY itself ('define policy for need-to-know') is organizational; Stave verifies the resulting access restrictions, not the policy definition.

controls.aicm_specification: When allowing model output modification of AI generated output, establish a role for this access and allow changes only by authorized identities.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. 'When allowing model output modification, establish a role and allow changes only by authorized identities.' The act of modifying AI-generated output and gating it to an authorized identity is an inference-time / application-runtime authorization event — it happens when output is produced and edited, not in any cloud-config snapshot. The closest config sliver would be an IAM role scoped to an output-modification action, but no such resource/property is exposed in infra config (there is no AWS/Azure/GCP 'model output modification' API surface to evaluate). Treated as runtime: no config property to check, so no Stave control should be built from a snapshot. The general least-privilege/role-scoping controls (IAM-05) apply to whatever role is created, but they do not verify this AI-specific output-modification semantics.

controls.aicm_specification: Restrict agents' access to the tools and plugins necessary for the activity or use case at hand, ensuring adherence to the principles of need-to-know and least privilege.
controls.notes: Restrict AGENTS' access to only the tools/plugins needed (need-to-know + least privilege for AI agents). Config-verifiable and directly modeled for Bedrock agents: execution role must scope bedrock:InvokeModel, lambda:InvokeFunction (tool invocation), and S3; action-group (tool/plugin) count must be bounded; knowledge-base role scoped to its data sources. This is exactly 'restrict agent access to necessary tools'. Partial, not full: coverage is Bedrock-specific. Agent frameworks outside Bedrock (e.g. self-hosted/LangChain-style agents, other providers' agent tool grants) have no equivalent control — a gap. A control checking per-agent allow-listed tool/plugin set against declared need would close it generally.

controls.aicm_title: Interoperability and Portability Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures for interoperability and portability including requirements for: a. Communications between application interfaces b. Information processing interoperability c. Application development portability d. Information/Data exchange, usage, portability, integrity, and persistence Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance control: establish/document/approve/communicate/review-annually policies and procedures for interoperability and portability. No technical configuration property is verifiable from an infrastructure snapshot. The annual-review and policy-existence requirements are human process artifacts.

controls.aicm_specification: Provide application interface(s) to service  customers so that they programmatically  retrieve their data to enable interoperability  and portability.
controls.notes: Provider-side product/architecture obligation: expose an API so customers can programmatically export their data. Stave evaluates a tenant's own infrastructure config snapshot, not whether a service provider ships a data-retrieval API. There is no resource property (encryption flag, policy setting, etc.) that proves an export API exists, so this is not config-verifiable. Designing a Stave control here would require an observation property like properties.service.data_export_api.enabled, which no current schema captures and which is a feature-availability assertion rather than a security posture.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement cryptographically secure network  protocols for the management, import and  export of data, according to industry  standards.
controls.notes: Config-verifiable: 'cryptographically secure network protocols for management, import and export of data' maps to Stave's broad encryption-in-transit family. Stave verifies TLS-version floors and HTTPS/SSL enforcement on the data and management surfaces that move customer data: API Gateway (TLS 1.2, custom-domain TLS, mTLS client certs), CloudFront viewer/origin HTTPS+TLS, S3-via-CloudFront origin HTTP detection, load balancers (HTTP->HTTPS redirect, TLS 1.2, weak-cipher policies, plaintext-to-backend), DMS migration endpoints (SSL/TLS for data import/export), EFS/ElastiCache/DocumentDB/DAX in-transit encryption, and the Azure/GCP/Cloudflare HTTPS+TLS equivalents. These are unsafe_state checks on properties like properties.loadbalancer.encryption.tls_1_2_or_higher and origin_uses_http. Marked PARTIAL not FULL: (1) Stave's coverage is per-service and tied to whichever services appear in the snapshot, so it cannot assert that ALL management/import/export channels are protected (e.g. SFTP/Transfer Family, SSH/SCP management planes, generic VPN/IPsec tunnels, on-host application protocols are not all covered); (2) 'according to industry standards' implies a defined cipher/protocol baseline that Stave enforces only where a dedicated control exists (e.g. ELB weak-cipher, CloudFront/Cloudflare TLS floors) and not uniformly across every endpoint. The TLS-floor + HTTPS-enforcement intent is well covered for the major data-transport surfaces.

controls.aicm_specification: Agreements must include provisions  specifying service customers' access to  data upon contract termination and will  include: a. Data format b. Length of time the data will be stored c. Scope of the data retained and made  available to the service customers d. Data deletion policy
controls.notes: Contractual control: agreements must specify post-termination data access, format, retention period, scope, and deletion policy. These are terms in a customer contract, not properties of a cloud configuration. Stave does have related posture controls for retention/lifecycle (e.g. log-group retention) but those verify a resource setting, not the contractual obligation; the AICM intent here is the existence of contract provisions, which is purely organizational.

controls.aicm_title: Infrastructure and Virtualization Security Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures for infrastructure and virtualization security. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually,  or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure policy-lifecycle control: establish, document, approve, communicate, review-annually policies for infrastructure and virtualization security. No technical configuration property to verify from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Plan and monitor the availability, quality, and adequate capacity of resources in order to deliver the required system performance as determined by the business.
controls.notes: Config-verifiable aspects covered well: auto-scaling presence/config, capacity alarms, throttling/quotas, resource quotas. The 'plan availability/quality as determined by the business' aspect is organizational/process and not snapshot-verifiable. Mapped controls confirm scaling and capacity-headroom configuration exists; they do not assess whether planned capacity meets business performance targets.

controls.aicm_specification: Monitor, encrypt and restrict communications between environments, services, and applications to only authenticated and authorized connections, as justified by the  business. Review these configurations at least annually, and support them by a documented justification of all allowed services, protocols, ports, and compensating controls.
controls.notes: Strong config coverage of restricting communications (security groups, NACLs, GCP firewall rules to authenticated/authorized ranges + ports) and encrypting communications (TLS/HTTPS enforcement, in-transit encryption across ELB, CloudFront, API Gateway, EFS, ElastiCache, DMS) plus monitoring (VPC flow logs). Not full: the AICM 'annual review with documented justification of all allowed services/protocols/ports/compensating controls' is an organizational/process requirement Stave cannot verify, and 'only authenticated and authorized connections' depends on app-layer authN that snapshots do not fully capture.

controls.aicm_specification: Harden host and guest OS, hypervisor or infrastructure control plane, according to their respective best practices, and supported by  technical controls, as part of a security baseline.
controls.notes: Host/guest OS and control-plane hardening config is broadly covered: IMDSv2 + hop limit, SSM management, patch currency, AMI currency/trust, Shielded VM, no-privileged/no-root/read-only-rootfs for containers and pods. Marked partial not full because 'according to their respective best practices as part of a security baseline' implies a full CIS-style benchmark; Stave checks key hardening flags but does not attest to a complete OS baseline, and hypervisor-level hardening (for self-managed virtualization) is largely the cloud provider's responsibility and not in a tenant snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Separate production and non-production environments to reduce the risk of sensitive production data being used in non-production environments. Production data is sanitized or protected before any authorized non-production use.
controls.notes: Production/non-production separation is well covered at the config layer: VPC env isolation, network env-mix, IAM cross-env access paths, and cross-env sharing of RDS/EBS snapshots and KMS keys. The specific requirement that 'production data is sanitized or protected before non-production use' (data masking/anonymization) is only partially observable: CTL.STEPFUNCTIONS.DEV.PROD.DATA.001 flags prod data in a dev workflow, but Stave has no general control verifying that copied/exported data was sanitized/masked. Gap: a control checking that non-prod datastores do not contain unmasked production/sensitive data.

controls.aicm_specification: Design, develop, deploy and configure applications and  infrastructures such that service customer (tenant) access  is appropriately segmented and segregated, monitored and  restricted.
controls.notes: Tenant/workload segmentation and segregation broadly covered: network tiering, east-west inspection, peering/TGW least-access routing, EKS namespace multi-tenancy + network policy enforcement, S3 prefix tenant isolation, SageMaker network isolation, KMS key isolation across sensitivity domains. Marked partial because the AICM 'monitored' aspect (per-tenant runtime access monitoring) is runtime and the spec's full application-layer multi-tenancy design cannot be wholly verified from infrastructure config; covered surfaces are config-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Use secure and encrypted communication channels when migrating  servers, services, applications, or data to hosted environments.  Such channels must include only up-to-date and approved protocols.
controls.notes: Migration channel encryption/up-to-date-protocol verifiable for the data-migration service: DMS enforces SSL/TLS, is not publicly accessible, and logs source/target; TLS-minimum controls confirm only current protocols on the relevant transport endpoints. Partial because Stave covers the DMS migration path and generic TLS endpoints but has no control specifically attesting that ALL server/service/application migration channels (e.g. DataSync, Snowball, Transfer Family, Application Migration Service) use only up-to-date approved protocols. Gap: explicit in-transit-encryption + approved-protocol checks for DataSync/Transfer Family/MGN endpoints.

controls.aicm_specification: Identify and document high-risk environments based on data sensitivity, threat exposure, and business impact.
controls.notes: Spec (per CAIQ) is to 'identify and document high-risk environments based on data sensitivity, threat exposure, and business impact' — a risk-classification/documentation exercise. No configuration property to verify from a snapshot; the act of identifying and documenting is a human/governance process. (Stave can label sensitive resources via tags but does not perform or attest to the risk-rating documentation itself.)

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and  defense-in-depth techniques for protection, detection, and timely  response to network-based attacks.
controls.notes: Defense-in-depth protection + detection is config-verifiable and broadly covered: AWS Network Firewall (stateful rules, non-permissive, in-path, logging, TLS inspection), DNS Firewall, Shield Advanced (DDoS), GuardDuty (threat detection/malware), WAF across ELB/API Gateway/CloudFront, and VPC flow logs for detection. Partial because 'timely response to network-based attacks' is a runtime incident-response process Stave cannot evaluate from a snapshot; Stave verifies the defensive controls are deployed/configured, not the response execution.

controls.aicm_title: Logging and Monitoring Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and  maintain policies and procedures for logging and monitoring. Review  and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance requirement: establish/document/approve/communicate/review-annually a logging and monitoring policy. No technical config artifact in a snapshot can prove a policy was authored and reviewed. Stave can verify the *implementation* of such a policy (see LOG-02/03/07/09/10), but the policy lifecycle itself is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to ensure the security and retention of audit logs.
controls.notes: Security + retention of audit logs is exactly Stave's strong suit, verified across providers. Security: log encryption (KMS/CMK), file-validation/integrity digests, deny-delete bucket policies, Object Lock/MFA-delete, public-access denial, cross-account replication. Retention: explicit >90d / >=365d / lifecycle-not-too-short checks plus GCP retention-lock and Azure activity-log retention. Covers the technical-measures portion comprehensively.

controls.aicm_specification: Identify and monitor security-related events within  applications and the underlying infrastructure. Define and  implement a system to generate alerts to responsible  stakeholders based on such events and corresponding  metrics.
controls.notes: Config-posture reading: the requirement is that a monitoring+alerting *system* be defined and implemented (metric filters/alarms wired to notification channels for security events). Stave has very deep coverage of whether the CIS security-event monitors, their alarms, and their notification actions are present and wired (not orphaned/disabled/no-action) across AWS/GCP/Azure. The act of stakeholders responding to live alerts is runtime/organizational and not in scope, but presence-of-monitoring is fully covered.

controls.aicm_specification: Restrict audit log access to authorized identities and maintain records of that access.
controls.notes: The 'restrict access to authorized identities' half is config-verifiable and well covered: broad/public read of the CloudTrail S3 bucket, unrestricted LookupEvents, public/cross-account CloudWatch log-group resource policies, and log-export destination restriction. The 'maintain records of that access' half is partly addressed by CTL.CLOUDWATCH.MONITOR.TRAIL.ACCESS.001 (alarm on unauthorized bucket access) but the accountability bookkeeping (who accessed logs and when) is data/process, not a static config property — hence partial.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement and maintain capabilities to correlate and monitor security audit logs for the detection of suspicious or anomalous activity that deviates from typical or expected patterns. Establish and follow a defined process to review and take appropriate and timely actions on detected anomalies.
controls.notes: Core requirement is real-time correlation/anomaly detection across logs and a follow-and-respond process. Detecting activity that 'deviates from typical patterns' is behavioral/runtime and cannot come from a static snapshot. Note: the *presence* of detection capability (GuardDuty enabled, CloudTrail Insights enabled, anomaly-monitoring metric filters) is config and is captured under LOG-03; this control's emphasis on the detect-and-respond behavior itself is runtime.

controls.aicm_specification: Use a reliable time source across all relevant information processing systems.
controls.notes: Time-source configuration is config-verifiable, and Stave checks NTP configuration on Cisco network devices, NTP on ESXi hosts, and Kerberos clock-skew tolerance. Partial because there is no cloud-native time-source check (e.g., EC2/Linux chrony or Amazon Time Sync Service usage). Gap: a control verifying that compute instances point at a reliable/authenticated NTP source. In managed cloud (Lambda/managed services) clock sync is provider-handled, so this is mostly relevant to self-managed VMs.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document and implement which information meta/data system events should be logged. Review and update the scope at least annually or whenever there is a change in the threat environment, and as per relevant regulatory requirements.
controls.notes: The 'implement which events are logged' half is config-verifiable and strongly covered: management+data event selectors (S3/Lambda/DynamoDB/EventBridge/Secrets/SNS/SQS), global service events, write-only-vs-read coverage, VPC/network flow logs, K8s/EKS control-plane audit, GCP audit logging, Azure activity-log export. Partial because the 'establish/document and review the scope annually' governance half is organizational and not snapshot-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate technical measures for service customers to detect and scrub or tokenize sensitive data from logs to prevent unauthorized exposure, as per applicable laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Config-verifiable measures that prevent sensitive data from reaching logs: API Gateway parameter-masking present when data tracing is on, execution logging not capturing full request/response bodies, the API-key header not being logged, plus Macie sensitive-data detection on storage. Partial because there is no generic log-scrubbing/tokenization control across all log sinks (e.g., CloudWatch Logs data-protection policies that mask PII). Gap: a control verifying CloudWatch Logs account/log-group data-protection (PII masking) policies are enabled.

controls.aicm_specification: Generate audit records containing relevant security information.
controls.notes: Whether audit records are generated, and (for API Gateway) whether the access-log *format* includes the critical security fields, is config-verifiable and covered. Partial/full boundary: Stave confirms logging is enabled and that one surface (API Gateway) has a complete field set, but it does not validate the field-level content of every record type (e.g., that CloudTrail/flow-log records carry all 'relevant security information'). The presence side is well covered; field-completeness is only checked for select surfaces.

controls.aicm_specification: Protect audit records from unauthorized access, modification, and  deletion.
controls.notes: Directly maps to Stave's tamper-protection controls: no-delete bucket policy, Object Lock (WORM), MFA-delete, log-file validation/digest integrity, encryption, restricted read, IAM/SCP guards against StopLogging/DeleteTrail, cross-account replication for an immutable copy, and GCP log-bucket retention lock. Protects against unauthorized access, modification, and deletion comprehensively.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and maintain a monitoring and internal reporting capability over the operations of cryptographic, encryption and key management  policies, processes, procedures, and controls.
controls.notes: The monitoring/reporting capability over crypto+key-management operations is config-verifiable as 'are the CloudWatch alarms for KMS key operations present?' Stave checks alarms for ScheduleKeyDeletion, DisableKey, PutKeyPolicy, CreateGrant, rotation failure/events, cross-account usage, decrypt failures/volume, plus CMK disable/deletion monitoring and Secrets-Manager rotation alarms. This is the snapshot-verifiable substance of an encryption-operations monitoring capability.

controls.aicm_specification: Log and monitor key lifecycle management events to enable auditing and reporting on usage of cryptographic keys.
controls.notes: KMS key lifecycle/usage events flow through CloudTrail (management events, covered by CloudTrail-enabled checks) and the requirement to log+monitor them is met by the KMS CloudWatch alarms for key creation-of-grants, deletion scheduling, disable, policy change, rotation, and cross-account/high-volume decrypt usage. Together these enable auditing and reporting on cryptographic-key usage as the spec requires.

controls.aicm_specification: Monitor and log physical access using an auditable access  control system.
controls.notes: Physical access logging (badge/door access control systems in datacenters). For cloud tenants this is inherited from the provider; there is no customer-controllable config artifact in an infrastructure snapshot. Physical-layer control with no technical config component visible to Stave.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures for the reporting of anomalies and failures of the monitoring  system and provide immediate notification to the accountable party.
controls.notes: The 'monitoring of the monitoring system' is well covered as config: alarms stuck in INSUFFICIENT_DATA, missing-data treated as not-breaching, alarms with no action / disabled / pointing at deleted SNS topics, metric filters with no alarm, subscription filters with no monitoring, Config delivery-failure monitoring, and detection that CloudTrail stopped logging plus an alarm on StopLogging — these detect failures/gaps in the monitoring pipeline itself. Partial because 'immediate notification to the accountable party' and the response process are runtime/organizational; Stave verifies the wiring (notification channel exists, not email-only, not single-topic blast radius) but not the act of notifying.

controls.aicm_specification: Log and monitor all input events (content and metadata) to enable auditing and reporting on the usage of AI models.
controls.notes: AI-Specific: the *config* property is whether model-invocation logging is enabled so input events are captured — CTL.BEDROCK.LOG.INVOCATION.001 checks properties.ai.logging.invocation_logging_enabled (captures request/response for InvokeModel/Converse/streaming) and CTL.BEDROCK.AGENT.LOGGING.001 checks per-agent invocation logging; log encryption protects the captured input. This is config-verifiable for Bedrock. Partial because: (1) it is scoped to Bedrock only — no equivalent input-logging config check for SageMaker endpoints or self-hosted model serving; and (2) the runtime 'monitor all input events for misuse' behavior is out of scope. The act of logging being *enabled* is config; analyzing the logged inputs is runtime.

controls.aicm_specification: Log and monitor all output events (content and metadata) to enable auditing and reporting on the usage of AI models.
controls.notes: AI-Specific: Bedrock invocation logging captures both request and response payloads, so the same config property (properties.ai.logging.invocation_logging_enabled) that satisfies input capture also captures output/response events; CTL.BEDROCK.AGENT.LOGGING.001 covers per-agent response logging and log-encrypt protects them. Config-verifiable for Bedrock. Partial because: (1) Bedrock-only — no SageMaker/self-hosted output-logging config check; and (2) the runtime side, monitoring output *content* (e.g., harmful/leaking responses) at inference time, is out of scope; that behavioral filtering belongs to guardrails/runtime, not a snapshot. Enabling the logging is config; inspecting outputs is runtime.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, and evaluate policies, procedures, and technical measures that ensure the security of the Training Pipeline. Regularly review and update policies, procedures and technical measures to address new security threats and best practices.
controls.notes: Mixed config + organizational (the spec demands policies/procedures plus technical measures, and 'regularly review/update' is process). The config-verifiable surface of a SageMaker training pipeline is well covered: training-volume encryption at rest, inter-container traffic encryption, encrypted data-source reads, cross-account data-source boundary, network isolation, VPC placement, scoped S3 and PassRole permissions on the training role, and PassRole-escalation guards on CreateTrainingJob/CreateProcessingJob. Partial because the organizational 'define/evaluate/review policies' component is out of scope for a snapshot evaluator, and the pipeline orchestration (e.g. Step Functions / pipeline DAG security) is only partially represented.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, and evaluate policies, procedures, and technical measures for the scanning of model artifacts for vulnerabilities and attacks, at each step of the service lifecycle and at each hand over point. Regularly review and update policies, procedures and technical measures to address model artifact scanning.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. The 'scanning enabled / findings acted on' aspect is a CONFIG property and is verifiable: ECR/ACR/Artifact-Registry image scanning toggles and unresolved-finding windows confirm that the container image carrying a model is scanned. MISSING: there is no Stave control that scans the MODEL ARTIFACT ITSELF (e.g. a pickle/safetensors/ONNX blob in S3 or the SageMaker model registry) for malicious deserialization payloads or model-specific attacks. Model artifacts are typically stored as S3 objects (ModelDataUrl), not container images, so ECR scanning only covers the container-packaged case. Gap: a control on the model-artifact store (S3 bucket / SageMaker Model Registry / Bedrock custom-model import) asserting an artifact-malware/deserialization scan ran (e.g. properties.ai.model_artifact.scanned == true). Also organizational on the 'define/review policies' side.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, enforce, approve, document, communicate, maintain and evaluate processes and procedures for model documentation. Regularly review and update the model documentation.
controls.notes: AI-Specific but purely PROCESS/DOCUMENTATION (model cards, datasheets, approval and review workflows). No configuration property of a cloud resource is asserted; existence and quality of model documentation cannot be derived from an infrastructure snapshot. Out of scope for Stave.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and implement baseline requirements for Model documentation.
controls.notes: AI-Specific, documentation-governance. 'Establish baseline requirements for model documentation' is a policy artifact, not a cloud config property. Out of scope for a snapshot evaluator.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures for the validation of the Model documentation aligned with the current model.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Validating that model documentation matches the currently deployed model is a process/behavioral activity (reconcile docs vs live model), not a static config property. The CAIQ question confirms it is about processes/procedures. No infrastructure snapshot can attest documentation-to-model alignment. Out of scope.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, and evaluate processes and technical measures to assess adversarial threats specific to each AI model.
controls.notes: AI-Specific and runtime/behavioral. Assessing adversarial threats (red-teaming, attack-surface analysis, probing the model with adversarial inputs) requires exercising the live model, not reading config. The closest Stave config defenses are Bedrock guardrail prompt-attack filters, but those are mitigations (MDS-07), not the threat-analysis process this control demands. Out of scope (runtime).

controls.aicm_title: Robustness against Adversarial Attack / Model Hardening
controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures for Model Hardening to mitigate relevant adversarial attacks as identified in the Threat Analysis and Adversarial Threat Analysis.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. Some hardening mitigations ARE config-verifiable: whether a Bedrock guardrail exists and is associated to an agent (guardrail_associated), whether the prompt-attack filter is at HIGH strength (prompt_attack_filter_high), and whether the sensitive-information/PII filter is enabled are all snapshot-readable config properties. Partial because true 'model hardening' (adversarial training, input sanitization at inference, output validation, robustness testing) is largely runtime/behavioral and process-driven; Stave only covers the Bedrock-guardrail configuration layer and has no SageMaker-side or generic model-hardening control.

controls.aicm_specification: Regularly calculate and compare checksums using cryptographic hashes of model checkpoints to detect unauthorized modifications. Apply at least annually based on the level of risk, or after any change of hands.
controls.notes: Config-verifiable portion closed: CTL.MODEL.INTEGRITY.CONFIG.001 requires the model store to have Object Lock + versioning + per-object checksums (and SageMaker ModelDataHashValue) — the infrastructure that ENABLES integrity comparison, the same proxy LOG controls use for audit. Partial, not full: the AICM requirement's periodic recompute-and-compare activity is runtime/behavioral and not snapshot-verifiable.

controls.aicm_specification: Sign models cryptographically and verify signatures to ensure model provenance and ownership, any time the model changes hands or is loaded from storage.
controls.notes: AI-Specific intent, config-verifiable property (signing enforcement is a static config flag). When the model is packaged as a container image, CTL.ECR.SIGNING.001 (AWS Signer/Notation/Cosign verification in enforce mode) covers signature verification on load. When packaged as a Lambda deployment artifact, CTL.LAMBDA.CODESIGN.ENFORCE.001/001 cover signed-package enforcement. Partial because these are container/Lambda code-signing surfaces, NOT direct model-artifact signing: a model stored as an S3 object (SageMaker ModelDataUrl) or in the Bedrock custom-model store has no Stave control verifying a cryptographic signature/provenance attestation. Gap: model-artifact signature-verification-on-load control for S3 model objects / SageMaker Model Registry / Bedrock imported models.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures for continuous monitoring of model performance metrics over time to identify sudden shifts or unexpected changes in predictions that could degrade model performance.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. The actual monitoring of prediction drift/shift over time is RUNTIME/behavioral, but the CONFIG precondition — that a SageMaker endpoint has a model-monitoring schedule attached (data quality, model quality, bias drift, feature attribution) — is snapshot-verifiable via CTL.SAGEMAKER.ENDPOINT.MONITOR.001 (properties.compute.governance.has_model_monitor). Partial: Stave confirms monitoring is configured but cannot evaluate the live performance metrics, and there is no Bedrock-side model-monitoring equivalent. The 'define/evaluate processes' part is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Perform a risk-based evaluation of the model and model serving infrastructure for model failure. Define and implement measures to mitigate model and model serving infrastructure failures, and regularly evaluate throughout the AI system's lifecycle.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. 'Model serving infrastructure failure' has a config-verifiable resilience dimension: CTL.SAGEMAKER.ENDPOINT.REDUNDANCY.001 (multiple instances behind an endpoint, removes single-instance failure point) and CTL.STEPFUNCTIONS.BEDROCK.NOQUOTA.001 (throttle/quota guard preventing serving overload) are static config properties; endpoint monitoring supports failure detection. Partial because 'model failure' as a property of the model's predictive behavior (not its infrastructure) is runtime, and the 'risk-based evaluation / regularly evaluate over lifecycle' part is organizational. Stave only covers the serving-infrastructure-resilience config slice.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish a process to evaluate risk associated with open models. Periodically review these risk factors, and implement a process to monitor and mitigate any determined vulnerabilities.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. 'Establish a process to evaluate risk of open (third-party/open-weight) models and periodically review' is a governance/process activity. While the mitigation outcome could touch config (scanning, network isolation), the control itself mandates a risk-assessment process, which is organizational and not derivable from a snapshot. Out of scope (organizational).

controls.aicm_specification: Adopt secure model formats and processes for AI model serialization where applicable.
controls.notes: Closed. The serialization format of a stored model artifact is a static, cloud-visible property; CTL.MODEL.FORMAT.INSECURE.001 fails pickle-family formats (pickle/pytorch_pickle/joblib) and passes safetensors/onnx/etc. Fully config-verifiable.

domains.domain: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics

controls.aicm_title: Security Incident Management Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures for Security Incident Management, E-Discovery,  and Forensics. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure policy lifecycle (establish/document/approve/communicate/review annually) for incident management, e-discovery, forensics. No technical config component; no snapshot property to verify.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and  maintain policies and procedures for the timely management of  security incidents. Review and update the policies and procedures at  least annually, or upon significant  changes.
controls.notes: Pure policy/procedure lifecycle for timely incident management. Organizational governance; nothing verifiable from a config snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy for notifying relevant internal departments, impacted service customers, and other business critical relationships (such as supply-chain) that may be impacted.
controls.notes: Establish/maintain an incident response PLAN including a communication/notification strategy. Human-process document; no config posture to evaluate.

controls.aicm_specification: Exercise the incident response plans at planned intervals or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Exercise (test) incident response plans at intervals. Tabletop/exercise activity; runtime/process, no static config artifact. Treated as organizational process.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, monitor and report information security incident metrics.
controls.notes: Establish/monitor/report incident metrics. Reporting/measurement process; no cloud-config property to check.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures supporting business processes to triage security-related events.
controls.notes: Define/implement/evaluate triage processes for security events. CAIQ frames this as process+procedures+supporting technical measures, but the verifiable object is an organizational triage workflow, not a snapshot property. Detection/alarm config (e.g. CloudTrail alarms) supports triage but the AICM control itself is about the process, not the detector config.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures for timely and effective response to security incidents in accordance with incident categories and severity levels. Review, update, and test processes and procedures at least annually.
controls.notes: Define/implement/test incident-response processes by category/severity, reviewed annually. The 'response' is runtime incident-handling execution governed by an organizational process; neither the live response action nor the process doc is a static config property. Out of scope as a process control.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement processes, procedures and technical  measures for security breach notifications. Report material  security breaches including any relevant supply chain  breaches, as per applicable SLAs, laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Define/implement breach-notification processes and report material breaches per SLA/law. Notification process + regulatory reporting; no config posture.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish and maintain a secure repository of security incident records. Regularly review the incident records to identify patterns, root causes, and systemic vulnerabilities, and implement relevant corrective measures.
controls.notes: Two aspects. (1) Config-verifiable forensic-readiness: the 'secure repository of security incident records' maps to immutable/retained/access-controlled log & evidence storage. Stave verifies object-lock/WORM (CTL.CLOUDTRAIL.S3.OBJECTLOCK.001, CTL.S3.LOG.BUCKET.LOCK.001, CTL.AZURE.STORAGE.IMMUTABILITY.001), MFA-delete/no-delete (CTL.S3.MFADELETE.001, CTL.CLOUDTRAIL.S3.MFADELETE.001, CTL.CLOUDTRAIL.S3.NODELETE.001), versioning (CTL.S3.LOG.BUCKET.VERSIONING.001), retention (CTL.S3.LOG.RETENTION.001, CTL.CLOUDTRAIL.RETENTION.001, CTL.GCP.STORAGE.RETENTION.001, CTL.GCP.LOGGING.BUCKET.RETENTION.001), not-public (CTL.S3.LOG.BUCKET.PUBLIC.001) and log-file integrity validation (CTL.CLOUDTRAIL.LOG.VALIDATION.001). (2) Organizational: the 'regularly review records to find patterns/root-causes and implement corrective measures' is a human review process Stave cannot evaluate. Partial: config tamper-resistance of the evidence store is covered for generic CloudTrail/S3 log buckets, but there is no Stave control that asserts a DEDICATED incident-records repository exists with these properties (it only checks the standard log/trail buckets), so coverage of 'incident records' specifically is incidental, plus the review process is out of scope.

controls.aicm_specification: Maintain points of contact for applicable regulation authorities, national and local law enforcement, and other legal jurisdictional authorities.  Review and update the points of contact at least annually.
controls.notes: Maintain points of contact for regulators/law-enforcement/legal authorities, reviewed annually. Contact-list maintenance; purely organizational.

domains.domain: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability

controls.aicm_title: Supply Chain Risk Management Policies and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain policies and procedures for supply chain risk management. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance: establish/document/review supply-chain risk-management policies annually. No cloud-configuration artifact to evaluate from a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and  maintain policies and procedures for the application of the Shared  Security Responsibility Model (SSRM) within the organization.  Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Establishing/maintaining SSRM policy documentation is a human process with no config component.

controls.aicm_specification: Apply, document, implement and manage the SSRM throughout the  supply chain.
controls.notes: Managing the Shared Security Responsibility Model across vendors is process/governance, not a config snapshot property.

controls.aicm_specification: Provide SSRM Guidance to the service customers detailing information about the SSRM applicability throughout the supply chain.
controls.notes: Customer-facing guidance/communication. No technical configuration to verify.

controls.aicm_specification: Delineate the shared ownership and applicability of all CSA AICM  controls according to the SSRM.
controls.notes: Documenting control ownership split between CSP and customer is a governance artifact, not a snapshot property.

controls.aicm_specification: Review and validate the SSRM documentation.
controls.notes: Periodic documentation review is a human process.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement, operate, and audit or assess the portions of the SSRM which the organization is responsible for.
controls.notes: While the actual customer-side controls (e.g. encryption, IAM, network) are config-verifiable elsewhere in the AICM, this STA control is about the governance act of implementing/operating/auditing the SSRM portion overall, not a specific resource property. Out of scope as an organizational meta-control.

controls.aicm_specification: Develop and maintain an inventory of all supply chain relationships.
controls.notes: An inventory of vendor/supplier relationships is a maintained register, not a cloud-resource configuration. Stave evaluates resource posture, not a business-relationship catalog.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement, and enforce a process for establishing a Bill of Material for the service supply chain. Review and update the Bill of Material at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: AI-Specific. The BOM-establishment PROCESS (define/review/update annually) is organizational and out of scope. The config-verifiable proxy — integrity and traceability of the artifacts that make up the service supply chain — IS covered: registry vulnerability scanning (ECR/ACR/GCP Artifact), enhanced scanning + unresolved-finding gating, image signing/signature-verification admission, tag immutability, digest pinning, trusted-registry enforcement, and repo dependency scanning. GAP / what's missing: Stave has NO control that actually generates, ingests, or validates a software/model Bill-of-Materials document itself, and nothing for AI-specific BOM components (training-dataset provenance, model-card/foundation-model lineage). A purpose-built control would need an observation property like asset.sbom_present / sbom_components[] (or model.training_data_provenance) on compute/registry assets and assert its presence, completeness, and freshness — that does not exist today. Marked partial because the artifact-integrity substrate is checkable but the BOM artifact and AI provenance lineage are not.

controls.aicm_specification: Periodically review risk factors associated with supply chain relationships.
controls.notes: Periodic risk review of vendor relationships is a recurring human process, not a config property.

controls.aicm_specification: Service agreements must incorporate at least the following  mutually-agreed upon provisions and/or terms:  • Scope, characteristics and location of business  relationship and services offered  • Information security requirements (including SSRM)  • Change management process  • Logging and monitoring capability  • Incident management and communication procedures  • Right to audit and third party assessment  • Service termination  • Interoperability and portability requirements  • Data privacy  • Operational Resilience
controls.notes: Contractual/SLA clause content. Entirely a legal/procurement artifact; nothing in a cloud snapshot proves contract terms.

controls.aicm_specification: Review supply chain agreements at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Periodic agreement review is a human process with no config component.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement a process for conducting internal assessments to confirm conformance and effectiveness of standards, policies,  procedures, and service level agreement activities at least annually.
controls.notes: Defining/running an internal assessment program is governance process, not a resource configuration.

controls.aicm_specification: Implement policies requiring all service providers throughout the supply chain to comply with information security, confidentiality, access control, privacy, audit, personnel policy and service level requirements and standards.
controls.notes: Policy requiring third-party compliance flow-down. The policy itself is organizational; provider compliance is attested contractually/by assessment, not from the org's own config snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Review the organization's service providers' IT governance policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Reviewing providers' governance documents is a human assessment activity.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement a process for conducting risk-based security assessments of the supply chain.
controls.notes: Defining a risk-based supplier-assessment process is governance. The assessment may USE config evidence about a provider, but this control concerns the org's own assessment program, which is not a snapshot property.

controls.aicm_title: Threat and Vulnerability Management Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures to identify, report and prioritize the remediation of vulnerabilities and threats, in order to protect systems against vulnerability exploitation. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Establish/document/approve/communicate/review-annually a TVM policy. Pure governance program; no static config artifact to verify.

controls.aicm_title: Malware and Malicious Instructions Protection Policy and Procedures
controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain policies and procedures to protect against malware and malicious instructions. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Establish/document/maintain a malware/malicious-instruction protection policy reviewed at least annually. Policy-level governance, not a config snapshot. (Note: technical malware-protection enablement is exercised under TVM-03/TVM-13, but TVM-02 itself is the policy document.)

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures for the detection of vulnerabilities on organizationally managed assets at least monthly.
controls.notes: Vulnerability-detection enablement across the estate is broadly config-verifiable: GuardDuty/Inspector/Security Hub/Defender enabled, container & registry scanning, dependency/secret scanning, SQL VA, patch-scan freshness. Stave confirms scanners are ON and in scope but cannot prove the org-mandated 'at least monthly' cadence end-to-end; freshness checks (patch-scan-stale) partially approximate it. Mark partial.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate threat analysis processes and procedures to identify, assess and review the threat landscape for Cloud and AI systems. Build threat models according to industry best practices to inform the risk mitigation strategy.
controls.notes: AI-Specific: define/implement threat-analysis processes and build threat models per best practices. This is an analytical/governance process (threat modeling, landscape review) with no config property to assert from a snapshot — config vs runtime: neither; it is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to update detection tools, threat signatures, and indicators  of compromise on a weekly, or more frequent basis.
controls.notes: Keep detection tools/signatures/IOCs updated weekly. Mostly a managed-service+process concern. Stave can assert agent/auto-provisioning health (Defender auto-provisioning on, SSM agent connected) as a proxy that update plumbing exists, but signature/IOC update cadence itself is not a snapshot property. Gap: a control asserting threat-feed/signature 'last updated within N days' freshness. Partial.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to identify updates for applications which use third party or open source libraries according to the organization's vulnerability management policy.
controls.notes: Identify updates for apps using third-party/OSS libraries. Stave verifies dependency scanning is enabled, unresolved critical/high image findings, CVE admission blocking, stale base images, and outdated engine versions — strong coverage of the detection side. It does not verify the remediation/update-application process itself (org policy). Partial.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures for the periodic performance of penetration testing by independent third parties.
controls.notes: Periodic penetration testing by independent third parties. Procedural engagement; no config artifact in a snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures based on identified risks to support scheduled and emergency responses to vulnerability identification.
controls.notes: Scheduled and emergency response processes for vulnerability identification. Process/runbook governance; freshness controls (e.g. CTL.EC2.INSPECTOR.FINDINGS.STALE.001) touch remediation timeliness but the SLA/response-schedule program itself is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Use a risk-based method for effective prioritization of vulnerability remediation using an industry recognized framework.
controls.notes: Risk-based prioritization of vulnerability remediation using a recognized framework (e.g. CVSS). Methodology/governance decision; no config property to assert. Stave records severity on findings (critical/high) but does not encode the prioritization framework.

controls.aicm_specification: Use a risk-based method for the prioritization and mitigation of threats, leveraging an industry-recognized framework to guide threat decision-making and protection measures.
controls.notes: Risk-based prioritization AND mitigation of threats, leveraging a framework to guide threat decision-making and active protection measures. The decision-making/mitigation is live incident response and runtime threat handling, not a static snapshot. (Detection enablement is already captured under TVM-03.)

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement a process for tracking and reporting  vulnerability identification and remediation activities that includes stakeholder notification.
controls.notes: Process for tracking and reporting vuln identification/remediation with stakeholder notification. Reporting workflow + notification process; CTL.GUARDDUTY.EXPORT.001 / CTL.EKS.ECR.SCAN.EXPORT.001 export findings but the tracking-and-notify process is organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, monitor and report metrics for vulnerability identification and remediation at defined intervals.
controls.notes: Establish, monitor and report vuln-management metrics at defined intervals. Metrics program/reporting cadence; no config snapshot property.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement processes, procedures and technical measures to  apply guardrails to the AI system. Continuously evaluate guardrails for changes in regulatory requirements  and risk scenarios.
controls.notes: AI-Specific guardrails. Config-verifiable portion is strong: Stave checks Bedrock agents have an associated guardrail and that guardrails enable high-strength prompt-attack and PII/sensitive-info filters — these are config properties (properties.ai.guardrail.*, properties.ai.agent.guardrail_associated). However the spec also requires 'continuously evaluate guardrails for changes in regulatory requirements and risk scenarios', which is a runtime/governance aspect not snapshot-verifiable. Partial.

controls.aicm_specification: Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and  maintain policies and procedures for all endpoints. Review and update the policies and procedures at least annually, or upon significant changes.
controls.notes: Pure governance: establish/document/approve/communicate/review-annually a policy. No technical config component verifiable from a cloud snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, document, apply and evaluate a list of approved services, applications and sources of applications (stores) acceptable for use by  endpoints when accessing or storing organization-managed data.
controls.notes: Maintaining an allow-list of approved apps/app-stores for user endpoint devices is an MDM/policy activity. Stave evaluates cloud resource config, not user-device application inventories; no observation surface for endpoint-installed software.

controls.aicm_specification: Define and implement a process for the validation of the endpoint device's compatibility with operating systems and applications.
controls.notes: A validation process for device/OS/app compatibility. Process-only; no cloud config artifact to evaluate.

controls.aicm_specification: Maintain an inventory of all endpoints used to store, access and process company data.
controls.notes: Inventory of user endpoint devices (laptops/phones/workstations). Stave has CTL.SSM.INVENTORY.RESTRICT.001 and CTL.S3.INVENTORY.001 but those govern AWS SSM/S3 inventory of cloud resources, not a register of user devices. No mapping: different asset class. A gap-fill would need an endpoint-device asset inventory source outside Stave's cloud-snapshot model.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to enforce policies and controls for all endpoints permitted  to access systems and/or store, transmit, or process organizational  data.
controls.notes: AICM targets enforced management of all user endpoints (MDM enrollment). The cloud-endpoint analog Stave can verify is that EC2 compute endpoints are enrolled in and reachable by a management plane: CTL.EC2.SSM.MANAGED.001 (ssm_managed=false fails) and CTL.EC2.SSM.AGENT.STALE.001 (registered but agent ConnectionLost). Only covers AWS cloud-VM endpoints, not user laptops/mobile, and only the enrollment/reachability facet, not full policy enforcement. Process/procedure aspects are organizational.

controls.aicm_specification: Configure all relevant interactive-use endpoints to require an automatic lock screen.
controls.notes: Per-device OS screen-lock/idle-timeout setting, enforced via MDM on user endpoints. Not a cloud-config property; nothing in a cloud snapshot exposes endpoint lock-screen state. CTL.AD.LOCK.* are Active Directory account-lockout (failed-login) thresholds, a different concept, not a match.

controls.aicm_specification: Manage changes to endpoint operating systems, patch levels, and/or applications through the company's change management processes.
controls.notes: Core requirement is a change-management process for OS/patch/app changes (organizational). Config-verifiable cloud-VM analog: CTL.EC2.SSM.MANAGED.001 ensures instances are patchable via Patch Manager, and CTL.EC2.AMI.CURRENCY.001 flags stale base images. These cover AWS server-VM patch posture, not user-endpoint OS patch levels, and do not verify the change-management workflow itself.

controls.aicm_specification: Protect information from unauthorized disclosure on managed  endpoint devices with storage encryption.
controls.notes: AICM means full-disk encryption on user endpoint devices (BitLocker/FileVault). Stave's cloud-endpoint analog is volume encryption-at-rest: CTL.WORKSPACES.ENCRYPT.001 (managed virtual-desktop root/user volumes — the closest match, WorkSpaces being a cloud user endpoint), plus CTL.EC2.EBS.ENCRYPT.001 and CTL.EC2.EBS.DEFAULT.001 for server volumes. Covers cloud-hosted endpoint/VM storage encryption only, not physical laptop/mobile disk encryption.

controls.aicm_specification: Configure managed endpoints with anti-malware detection and prevention technology and services.
controls.notes: AICM means endpoint AV/EDR on user devices. Stave's cloud-VM analog: CTL.GUARDDUTY.MALWARE.PROTECT.001 verifies GuardDuty malware scanning of EBS volumes on EC2/ECS is enabled, and CTL.AZURE.DEFENDER.SERVERS.001 verifies Defender for Servers (threat protection) on Azure VMs. These verify that a malware-detection service is enabled for cloud compute, not that AV agents run on user laptops/phones. CTL.M365.DEFENDER.MALWARE.001 is email-attachment filtering, not endpoint AV, so excluded.

controls.aicm_specification: Configure managed endpoints with properly configured software firewalls.
controls.notes: Host-based/software firewall running on the endpoint OS (Windows Firewall, iptables/ufw on a laptop), enforced via MDM. Stave evaluates network-layer firewalls/security groups for cloud resources (e.g. CTL.AZURE.FIREWALL.*, SG controls), which is a network-perimeter concept, not the host software-firewall state of a user endpoint. No mapping; out of Stave's cloud-snapshot reach.

controls.aicm_specification: Configure managed endpoints with Data Loss Prevention (DLP) technologies and rules in accordance with a risk assessment.
controls.notes: Endpoint DLP runs as an agent on managed user devices (laptops/phones) deployed via MDM — not a cloud resource visible in an obs.v0.1 snapshot. Same class as UEM-10 (host software firewall), which is correctly out-of-scope. Unlike a CloudTrail trail or an S3 bucket, there is no cloud-config proxy Stave can read, so this is out of scope (organizational/endpoint-management), not an in-scope gap.

controls.aicm_specification: Enable remote geo-location capabilities for all managed mobile endpoints,  according to all applicable laws and regulations.
controls.notes: Mobile MDM geo-location capability on user devices. No cloud-config artifact; purely an endpoint/MDM feature outside Stave's domain.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical measures to enable the deletion of company data remotely on managed endpoint devices.
controls.notes: Remote-wipe capability for user endpoint devices via MDM. No cloud-config property; the deletion action and capability live in the device-management plane, not in a cloud resource snapshot.

controls.aicm_specification: Define, implement and evaluate processes, procedures and technical and/or contractual measures to maintain proper security of third-party endpoints with access to organizational assets.
controls.notes: Contractual/process measures governing third-party (vendor/contractor) endpoint security. Vendor-attestation and contract terms; no cloud-config artifact Stave can evaluate.
